shardPurpose: Evidence shard for D3-D10 architecture workstream. Lead merges into data/evidence-index.json.
retrievalMethod: web_search followed by web_fetch of the exact URL; only records whose URL returned HTTP 200 during the 2026-11-02 session are classed as retrieved. Records 017 and 019 document retrieval failures and assert no parameter from the failed page.

evidence.supportedAssertion: NMEA states that all products that read and/or transmit NMEA 2000 information must be certified by NMEA, that the NMEA 2000 standard is a registered trademark, that certification is based on the NMEA 2000 License Agreement and produces a mandatory encrypted certification file that NMEA validates before certification is granted, and that use of the official NMEA 2000 logo and the term 'NMEA 2000 Certified' follows validation.
evidence.limitations: Association webpage summary, not the licensed standard text; no fee schedule for NMEA 2000 licensing was printed on the page. Applies to entities that implement NMEA 2000; MAREA implements none.

evidence.supportedAssertion: NMEA states that each manufacturer must purchase a NMEA 2000 Manufacturer code issued by NMEA and that manufacturer code assignments take up to 60 days, and that a unique NMEA 2000 Product code must be purchased for each certified product.
evidence.limitations: No fee amount is printed on the page; lead time is stated as 'up to 60 days' by the association and is not a contractual availability commitment to MAREA.

evidence.supportedAssertion: NMEA states that the NMEA 0183 Interface Standard is a copyrighted document available only from NMEA, defines a 4800-baud serial data bus with one talker and multiple listeners, is not sold through an online store, and lists prices of USD 1,150 (NMEA manufacturer member), USD 7,500 (government/industrial/testing) and USD 10,000 (consumer electronics); latest version is 4.30 and NMEA 0183-HS defines 38.4 kbaud.
evidence.limitations: Prices are the published USD price list for the standard document, not a MAREA quotation; no purchase was made and no member discount was confirmed as available to MAREA.

evidence.supportedAssertion: NMEA states that an NMEA 0183 Manufacturer Mnemonic Code carries an administrative fee of USD 200, requires purchase of the standard at the applicable industry-group price, and is issued to companies only, not individuals.
evidence.limitations: Association webpage statement; no application was filed in MC-11.

evidence.supportedAssertion: Raspberry Pi 5 (launch announcement) has a 2.4 GHz quad-core 64-bit Arm Cortex-A76 CPU, VideoCore VII GPU, dual 4Kp60 HDMI, dual-band 802.11ac Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 5.0/BLE, Gigabit Ethernet, two USB 3.0 and two USB 2.0 ports, PCIe 2.0 x1, a standard 40-pin GPIO header and a real-time clock; peak power consumption is stated as around 12 W for pathological workloads and a 5 V/5 A (25 W) USB-C supply mode exists.
evidence.limitations: Announcement webpage, not the product datasheet; no operating-temperature range, ingress rating, vibration or EMC qualification is published on that page. Peak-power wording is approximate and not a measured product figure.

evidence.supportedAssertion: Raspberry Pi 5 is announced at USD 60 for the 4 GB variant and USD 80 for the 8 GB variant, plus local taxes.
evidence.limitations: Manufacturer launch price observation (HISTORICAL_OBSERVATION class); not a distributor price, not a MAREA cost, and the page is not a current price list. No price was retrieved for a current SKU in this session.

evidence.supportedAssertion: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 is a USD 5 microcontroller board built on RP2350 with two 150 MHz Arm Cortex-M33 cores, 520 KB on-chip SRAM, 4 MB external QSPI flash, signed-boot support, 8 KB antifuse OTP, SHA-256 acceleration and a hardware TRNG; it is form-factor and electrically compatible with the original Pico.
evidence.limitations: Launch announcement; no absolute-maximum ratings, temperature range, ADC accuracy or EMC data on the page. RP2350 datasheet was not retrieved in this session.

evidence.supportedAssertion: RP2350 variants are offered in a 7x7 mm QFN60 package (RP2350A, 30 GPIOs) or 10x10 mm QFN80 package (RP2350B, 48 GPIOs), with RP2354A/B adding 2 MB stacked QSPI flash; RP2350A is stated at USD 0.80 in 3,400-unit reels and USD 1.10 single-unit.
evidence.limitations: Announcement quantity-tier prices; no current distributor price was retrieved and no MAREA purchase occurred.

evidence.supportedAssertion: The Digital Yacht iKonvert is a bidirectional NMEA 2000 to USB converter that is powered from the NMEA 2000 network, provides full galvanic isolation between the USB interface and the NMEA 2000 network, uses an FTDI USB interface, operates at 230 kbaud in RAW PGN mode and 4.8/38.4/115 kbaud in NMEA 0183 conversion modes, and can send data (for example routes and waypoints) back onto the NMEA 2000 network where the software supports it.
evidence.limitations: Vendor product page; isolation type/voltage and transient ratings are not printed; no independent test. Used as a third-party comparator and as a design caution (bidirectional write path), never as a MAREA component.

evidence.supportedAssertion: The Toradex Verdin iMX8M Plus system-on-module uses an NXP i.MX 8M Plus with up to four 1.6 GHz Arm Cortex-A53 cores plus a 800 MHz Cortex-M7F, up to 8 GB LPDDR4 and up to 32 GB eMMC, two Gigabit Ethernet interfaces, 2.4/5 GHz 2x2 Wi-Fi 5 and Bluetooth 5.3 on wireless variants, two CAN FD interfaces, four UARTs, five I2C and three SPI, and is specified for -40 to +85 degrees C operation.
evidence.limitations: Vendor module page (returned in Chinese localisation); no carrier-board or enclosure qualification, no EMC certificate, no price other than the vendor's evaluation-kit amount. Wireless variants need their own radio conformity.

evidence.supportedAssertion: Toradex publishes a minimum product commitment of 2036+ for the Verdin iMX8M Plus variants shown on the page and states that several variants are in mass production.
evidence.limitations: Vendor lifecycle declaration, not a contractual supply guarantee to MAREA; variants differ (one shown as sample-only, one in development).

evidence.supportedAssertion: The STM32H743ZI is an Arm Cortex-M7 microcontroller at up to 480 MHz with up to 2 MB dual-bank flash and 1 MB RAM, a 1.62 to 3.6 V application supply and I/Os, two CAN controllers with CAN FD, two watchdogs (independent and window), an RTC, three ADCs and an Ethernet MAC, with 2.95 microamps in Standby mode; ST lists the product as active and in volume production.
evidence.limitations: Vendor product page; no price retrieved, no package-specific thermal data, no EMC data. 'In volume production' is a vendor lifecycle statement.

evidence.supportedAssertion: The u-blox MAX-M10 series are M10 standard-precision GNSS modules with stated power consumption below 25 mW, concurrent reception of major GNSS constellations, UART and I2C interfaces, a supply range of 1.76 to 3.6 V (5.5 V maximum on some variants) and an operating temperature range of -40 to +85 degrees C; the page lists several MAX-M10 variants including MAX-M10S-00B as 'not longer available'.
evidence.limitations: Vendor page; availability wording indicates end-of-life on listed order codes at the time of retrieval, and no successor part number was confirmed. Sensitivity, TTFF and antenna requirements were not retrieved.

evidence.supportedAssertion: The Microchip ATECC608B secure element supports ECC-P256 ECDH/ECDSA, SHA-256, AES-128-GCM, protected storage for up to 16 keys/certificates, a 72-bit unique serial number, I2C or single-wire interfaces, 1.8-5.5 V IO, 2.0-5.5 V supply, 0.03 microamps typical standby and operating temperature up to 100 degrees C; the page marks the device 'Not Recommended for new designs'.
evidence.limitations: Vendor lifecycle status is the material finding: the part is not recommended for new designs at retrieval date. No successor was confirmed from the page. Security claims are vendor claims and no evaluation was performed.

evidence.supportedAssertion: Directive 2014/53/EU (Radio Equipment Directive) applies to equipment that intentionally emits or receives radio waves for radio communication or radiodetermination; recital 6 states that all such equipment should fall within scope and recital 11 addresses receiver performance, so a receive-only radio receiver is radio equipment under the directive. The directive was in force with a current consolidated version dated 30/05/2026 at retrieval.
evidence.limitations: Legal text quoted for scope only; applicability to a specific MAREA configuration, the choice of conformity-assessment module and the current consolidated wording are reserved to the conformity workstream and qualified legal review. No conformity assessment was performed.

evidence.supportedAssertion: Annex I of Directive 2014/53/EU excludes from its scope marine equipment falling within the scope of Council Directive 96/98/EC (the predecessor Marine Equipment Directive), which is relevant when deciding whether a marine radio product is assessed under the RED or under the marine equipment regime.
evidence.limitations: The exclusion is quoted as published in 2014 and refers to Directive 96/98/EC; the MED has since been replaced by Directive 2014/90/EU, so the exact current interaction must be confirmed by the conformity workstream and qualified review. No applicability determination is made here.

evidence.limitations: Launch announcement wording; third-party OS support exists but is not first-party. No long-term support duration is stated on the page.
